hints.text: A parallelogram just needs both pairs of opposite sides parallel. A rhombus needs that PLUS four equal sides.
The shape with the extra rule always belongs to the bigger group, not the other way around.
Rhombuses have the extra rule, so all rhombuses are parallelograms.

explanation: A rhombus has both pairs of opposite sides parallel AND four equal sides, so it satisfies every parallelogram rule — statement B is true.
Statement A fails because a long parallelogram can have unequal sides, so it is not a rhombus.
Statement C fails because a trapezoid needs only one pair of parallel sides and need not have right angles.
Statement D fails because a kite is a quadrilateral with no parallel sides at all.

alternativeExplanations.title: One counterexample is enough
steps: To knock out "all parallelograms are rhombuses," just picture a slanted $2$-by-$5$ parallelogram.
Its sides are not equal, so it is not a rhombus — statement A is dead.
